title: Change-order impact coordinator

stages.name: reconstructInstruction
stages.algorithm: Reconcile site notes, messages, and drawing annotations to identify the actual requested action and its issuer. Distinguish clarification, proposed change, and authorized instruction; preserve conflicting versions and do not infer commercial authority from site presence.
stages.gate: Instruction scope and authority are separately evidenced.

stages.name: compareScope
stages.algorithm: Compare the instruction with the agreed baseline and approved prior changes. Identify additions, omissions, substitutions, or clarifications, preserve exclusions, and avoid treating a contractor’s preferred method as contractual scope unless the baseline supports it.
stages.gate: Each claimed change maps to a specific baseline requirement or omission.

stages.name: traceDependencies
stages.algorithm: Trace design, procurement, trade interfaces, and schedule dependencies using exact project graphs. Judge which dependencies are materially affected, distinguish potential from confirmed delay, and identify evidence needed to support commercial or timing claims.
stages.gate: Claimed downstream effects have dependency paths and explicit assumptions.

stages.name: formOptions
stages.algorithm: Construct feasible alternatives such as resequencing, substitution, or phased completion within approved design constraints. Obtain exact estimates from authorized services, disclose assumptions, and preserve professional review requirements for structural or safety consequences.
stages.gate: Option is technically reviewable, commercially explicit, and dependency-feasible.

stages.name: assembleChange
stages.algorithm: Prepare a coordinated scope, cost, timing, and responsibility package with the relevant evidence. Separate agreed changes from disputed claims, bind approvals to the exact revision, and update downstream plans only after the appropriate authorities accept the change.
stages.gate: No unapproved scope or schedule change silently enters the committed baseline.

operational_details: A verbal instruction is later disputed: preserve contemporaneous evidence and request formal confirmation.
A drawing revision changes only one area: avoid applying it to the whole project.
Work began before commercial approval: record actual events without backdating authority.
A delay claim ignores available float: use exact schedule analysis and explicit assumptions.
Two changes affect the same work: prevent duplicate cost attribution.
